claim_formal: ∃ finitely generated (torsion-free) discrete group G such that the coefficient-free reduced Baum–Connes assembly map μ_G fails to be an isomorphism (non-surjective via an irrational-trace projection; separately, a torsion-free example with an infinite-order kernel class)

quote_A.text: we construct a finitely generated torsion-free discrete group whose degree-zero assembly map has a kernel class of infinite order

quote_B.text: This disproves the coefficient-free reduced Baum–Connes conjecture for countable discrete groups.

notes: Three manuscripts: BC injectivity failure (torsion-free), BC surjectivity failure (irrational trace projection), and a torsion-free group with nontrivial projection in C*_r disproving Kadison–Kaplansky (also P1/O2/M3). Headline taken as the BC disproof per title/summary order.

claim_formal: ∀ Γ ∈ 𝒦 (ICC, commensurable with property-(T) lattice over char-0 local fields), ∀ countable ICC Λ, ∀ cocycles μ, ω, ∀ bifinite L_μ(Γ)–L_ω(Λ) correspondence H: ∃ finitely many models E(A,B,δ,σ) (finite-index subgroup isomorphisms δ, projective reps σ) with H ≅ closed summand of ⊕ E(A,B,δ,σ)

quote_A.text: Every such correspondence is a closed summand of a finite direct sum of models obtained from actual finite-index subgroup isomorphisms and finite-dimensional projective representations

quote_B.text: his later problems ask whether nonisomorphic ICC property-(T) groups have nonisomorphic factors

notes: Headline is a classification of bifinite bimodules (arithmetic exhaustion); the stable recovery theorem (L_ω(Λ)^t ≅ L_ν(Π)^s iff t=s and groups/cocycles match) is a corollary-level consequence addressing Connes' rigidity problem / Popa's stable formulation for the lattice class 𝒦. B coded as Connes rigidity restricted to class 𝒦 (O5); could alternatively be P5/O1 if the bimodule classification is viewed as a new result with no posed problem.

claim_formal: ∀ r, s ∈ (1, ∞]: L(F_r) ≅ L(F_s) as tracial von Neumann algebras (in particular L(F_2) ≅ L(F_3)); hence F(L(F_∞)) = ℝ_{>0}

quote_A.text: theorem allInterpolatedIsomorphic (r s : ℝ≥0∞) (hr : 1<r) (hs : 1<s) : Nonempty (NormalTracialEquiv ...)

quote_B.text: We solve the free group factor isomorphism problem affirmatively by proving that L(F_2) and L(F_3) are isomorphic

notes: Core constructive theorem is the closed statement L(F_2) ≅ L(F_3) (prefix none); Lean comparator and summary state the ∀ r,s form via the Dykema–Rădulescu dichotomy (prior result). Corollary: Voiculescu's free entropy dimension invariance question answered negatively. Isomorphism problem has no predicted answer (P2); arguably P1 if read as a conjecture of non-isomorphism, in which case outcome would flip to O2.

claim_formal: ∀ unital C*-algebra A, ∀ Hilbert space H, ∀ bounded unital homomorphism π: A → B(H), ∃ invertible S ∈ B(H) such that S π(·) S⁻¹ is a *-homomorphism

quote_A.text: There exists an operator S∈B(H), invertible with bounded inverse, such that ρ(a)=Sπ(a)S^{-1} (a∈A) is a *-homomorphism.

quote_B.text: This resolves Kadison's similarity conjecture positively.

notes: Matrix could be read as M1 (property 'similar to a *-hom' holds for every π); coded M2 following the 342 convention for ∀∃ existence of a witness. Proof goes through a universal commutator estimate (M8, ∃C ∀...) and Kirchberg's similarity–derivation equivalence; corollary: universal hyperreflexivity constant. Lean comparator states SimilarityTheorem directly.

claim_formal: ∀ ε>0 ∃ δ>0 ∀ Hilbert space H ∀ unital von Neumann algebras M,N ⊆ B(H): d_KK(M,N) < δ → ∃ unitary u with uMu* = N ∧ ‖u − I‖ < ε

quote_A.text: For every ε>0 there is δ=δ(ε)>0 such that ... there is a unitary u∈B(H) satisfying uMu^*=N, ‖u−I_H‖<ε.

quote_B.text: This resolves the strong Kadison–Kastler conjecture.

notes: Matrix could be M1 (uniform stability property); the conclusion asserts existence of a near-identity conjugating unitary. Two companion papers give counterexamples showing sharpness: one-sided near inclusions without small spatial embeddings (negative answer to CCSSWW question, M3/P2/O2) and close separable C*-algebras not spatially conjugate (disproves separable C*-spatial form, M3/O2).

claim_formal: ∀ unital inclusion N ⊂ M of von Neumann algebras with separable preduals and faithful normal conditional expectation: ∃ amenable P ⊂ N with faithful normal expectation F: N → P such that P' ∩ c(M) = N' ∩ c(M)

quote_A.text: There exist a unital amenable von Neumann subalgebra P⊂N and a faithful normal conditional expectation F:N→P such that P'∩c(M)=N'∩c(M).

quote_B.text: Marrakchi formulated the relative bicentralizer conjecture and proved that, for separable preduals, it is equivalent to the conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}. Our theorem therefore resolves that conjecture positively

notes: Headline taken as the relative bicentralizer conjecture (title leads with it). Summary first states Connes' (absolute) bicentralizer conjecture ∀ III_1 factor M ∀ φ: BC(M,φ)=ℂ1 (∀, M1); the second manuscript calls its proof of that an 'alternative proof' since Houdayer–Marrakchi announced it, so the absolute case would be O9. Lean comparator formalizes the bounded spectral recovery theorem, an intermediate analytic result (hence 'different').

claim_formal: ∀ simple separable unital infinite-dimensional nuclear stably finite Z-stable C*-algebra A, ∀ countable discrete amenable G, ∀ action α: G → Aut(A): ∃ cocycle conjugacy (Φ, u) between α and α ⊗ id_Z on A ⊗ Z

quote_A.text: absorbs the trivial action on the Jiang–Su algebra up to cocycle conjugacy

quote_B.text: This proves the unital, stably finite case of Szabó's Conjecture A on automatic equivariant Jiang–Su stability.

notes: Matrix could be M1 (action is equivariantly Z-stable). Bundled: strict comparison ⇒ Z-stability for separable simple nuclear non-elementary algebras (Toms–Winter implication, P1/O1, incl. nonunital); nonsimple equivalence dim_nuc<∞ ⇔ Z-stable (Robert–Tikuisis Conjecture C1); dim_nuc(A⊗Z) ≤ 1; answer to STW Problem XXI (real rank zero ⇒ uniform property Γ) and Kirchberg–Rørdam Question 6.2. Lean comparator (UniformGamma) formalizes the Problem XXI result, not the headline.

claim_formal: ∃ separable unital C*-algebra A (= C*(ℤ[1/2]^3 ⋊ (SL_3(ℤ)×ℤ))) ∀ nonzero unital nuclear B ∀ free ultrafilter ω: ¬∃ unital embedding A ↪ B^ω (in particular A ↪̸ O_2^ω)

quote_A.text: We construct an explicit separable unital full group C∗-algebra that admits no unital embedding into Bω, for any nonzero unital nuclear C∗-algebra B and any free ultrafilter ω on ℕ.

quote_B.text: We give a negative answer to Kirchberg's norm-ultrapower embedding problem.

notes: Counterexample to a universal question (tie-break 5 → M3). Witness is explicit but newly constructed, so prefix starts with ∃ (tie-break 1). Lean MainStatementWithCuntzCorollary matches the theorem including the O_2 specialization.

claim_formal: ∀ infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space H ∃ T ∈ B(H), T ≠ 0, norm-quasinilpotent, with no nonzero proper closed hyperinvariant subspace (commutant {T}' is a proper SOT-closed transitive algebra)

quote_A.text: theorem main_theorem (hInf : ¬FiniteDimensional ℂ H) : FullClaim (H := H) — ∃ T, T ≠ 0 ∧ ... ∧ TransitiveCommutant T ∧ commutant T ≠ ⊤

quote_B.text: We give a negative answer to the hyperinvariant-subspace problem by constructing, on every infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space, a nonzero bounded norm-quasinilpotent operator with no nonzero proper closed hyperinvariant subspace.

notes: Counterexample to the hyperinvariant-subspace question (tie-break 5 → M3). Also: negative answer to whether every transitive SOT-closed unital algebra is dense in B(H) (transitive algebra problem), and a weighted irrational rotation in the hyperfinite II_1 factor with no nontrivial invariant projection, answering Zhu–Fang–Shi negatively for every irrational angle. Several Lean comparators; HyperinvariantSubspaces matches the headline.

claim_formal: ∃ separable unital C*-algebra A admitting a normalized 2-quasitrace, ∃ positive contractions a,b ∈ A: ∀ normalized 2-quasitrace τ on A, τ(a+b) − τ(a) − τ(b) ≥ 1/144 (so no 2-quasitrace on A is a trace)

quote_A.text: There exist a separable unital complex C^*-algebra A, admitting a normalized 2-quasitrace, and positive contractions a,b∈A such that every normalized 2-quasitrace τ on A satisfies τ(a+b)−τ(a)−τ(b)≥1/144.

quote_B.text: We refute Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture by constructing a separable unital complex C∗-algebra that admits normalized 2-quasitraces but has no tracial state.

notes: Prefix could be read ∃∀ (∀ quasitraces τ); coded ∃ since the ∀τ is the property of the witness. Corollaries (via Milhøj–Rørdam equivalence): minimal tensor product of two unital simple stably finite C*-algebras (one = C*_r(F_2)) can be properly infinite, negative answer to Milhøj–Rørdam Question 2.5; a separable stably finite algebra with no tracial state. Equivalent to a negative answer to Kaplansky's AW*-factor question.

claim_formal: ∀ complex von Neumann algebra M ∀ k ≥ 2 ∀ bounded k-cocycle f ∈ C_b^k(M,M) with df = 0: ∃ g ∈ C_b^{k−1}(M,M) with f = dg (i.e. H_b^k(M,M) = 0)

quote_A.text: Every f∈C_b^k(M,M) satisfying df=0 has the form f=dg for some g∈C_b^{k-1}(M,M). Consequently H_b^k(M,M)=0.

quote_B.text: Together with the established degree-one inner-derivation theorem, this resolves the Kadison–Ringrose cohomology conjecture positively.

notes: Matrix ambiguous between M2 (existence of a bounded primitive for each cocycle) and M1/M7 (H_b^k(M,M)=0 vanishing). Full conjecture (all k≥1) needs the Kadison–Sakai degree-one theorem, hence full_only_with_prior_results.

claim_formal: ∀ type II_1 factor M with separable predual ∃ x ∈ M: M = W*(x) (equivalently M is generated by two self-adjoint elements)

quote_A.text: Every type II_1 factor M with separable predual is generated by two self-adjoint elements. Equivalently, there is an x∈M such that M=W^*(x).

quote_B.text: Combined with the established direct-integral reduction to this case, this gives an affirmative solution of the generator problem for von Neumann algebras with separable predual.

notes: Generator problem is posed for all separable-predual von Neumann algebras; the II_1-factor case plus Willig's direct-integral reduction (prior result) gives the full answer. Stronger relative theorem: for irreducible P ⊂ M, generators u with M = W*(P,u) form a dense G_δ (∀ᵍ-type genericity; separate Lean comparator RelativeGeneration). FactorGeneration Lean matches the headline.

claim_formal: ∃ unital infinite-dimensional simple C*-algebra A with a faithful tracial state such that all nonzero irreducible representations of A are unitarily equivalent (hence A ≇ K(H)), in ZFC

quote_A.text: We construct in ZFC a unital infinite-dimensional simple complex C∗-algebra with a faithful tracial state whose nonzero irreducible representations are all unitarily equivalent.

quote_B.text: Tanaka gives another ZFC construction with a faithful tracial state ... so the existence conclusion of Theorem~\ref{na:main} is already present there. ... Here we give an alternative proof

notes: Negative answer to Naimark's problem in ZFC (would be P2/O2), but tie-break 9 applies: Tanaka's earlier ZFC construction already gives the existence conclusion, so O9 (new proof). Earlier counterexamples needed ◇ (Akemann–Weaver).

claim_formal: ∃ n ≥ 2 ∃ bounded self-adjoint tuple X = (X_1..X_n) in a tracial von Neumann algebra: −∞ < χ(X) ≤ χ*(X) − 1/2 < ∞

quote_A.text: There exist an integer n≥2 and a bounded self-adjoint tuple X=(X_1,…,X_n) ... such that −∞<χ(X)≤χ^*(X)−1/2<∞.

quote_B.text: We answer the finite-entropy equality question for microstates and nonmicrostates free entropy negatively.

notes: Posed problem: Voiculescu's unification question, stated explicitly as Guionnet's Conjecture 7.1 (χ>−∞ ⇒ χ=χ*); coded P1 because of the explicit conjecture, P2 also defensible (outcome O2 either way). Number of variables is large but fixed; smaller n not addressed.

claim_formal: ∀ nonzero unital separable C*-algebra A ∀ free ultrafilter ω: (F_ω(A) has no characters) ⇔ A ≅ A ⊗_min Z

quote_A.text: F_ω(A) has no characters ⟺ A≅A⊗_min Z.

quote_B.text: Kirchberg and Rørdam asked whether the absence of characters on F_ω(A) characterizes Jiang--Su absorption among unital separable C^*-algebras ... We prove the proposed characterization.

notes: Kirchberg–Rørdam Question 3.1, also listed as Problem LXXX in the Schafhauser–Tikuisis–White problem collection (could be argued P3; coded P2 since the collection repeats the KR question, tie-break 8). Proof via finite theorem: characterless D ⇒ unital I(2,3) → D^{⊗max m} plus Kirchberg–Rørdam Theorem 2.5. Corollary: infinite minimal tensor power of characterless D is Z-stable (answers Dadarlat–Toms question).

claim_formal: ∀ 0<ε<1 ∃ r_ε ≤ 5·10^8 ε^{-2} ∀ von Neumann algebra M ⊆ B(H), ∀ MASA A ⊆ M, ∀ x = x* ∈ M: x is (ε, r_ε) strong-operator pavable over A (∀ finite F ⊂ H, δ>0 ∃ partition P of size r_ε in A, a ∈ A, projection q with ‖(1−q)ξ‖<δ on F and ‖q(S_P(x)−a)q‖ ≤ ε‖x‖)

quote_A.text: every self-adjoint element of a von Neumann algebra admits strong-operator paving over each maximal abelian subalgebra with at most 5×10^8 ε^{-2} projections

quote_B.text: We prove the quadratic strong-operator paving conjecture of Popa and Vaes.

notes: Matrix ambiguous: M8 (quadratic upper bound O(ε^{-2}) on the paving size is the content of the 'quadratic' conjecture) vs M2 (existence of pavings). Companion paper proves Popa–Vaes approximation-paving conjecture (Conj. 2.8(1)) with C ε^{-6} projections; corollary: quadratic norm paving in Ocneanu ultrapowers for expected countably decomposable MASAs.

claim_formal: ∀ separable nuclear C*-algebras A, B: T(A) ≅ T(B) as topological cones → A ⊗ W ⊗ K ≅ B ⊗ W ⊗ K (realizing the given cone map)

quote_A.text: the canonical topological cone of all extended lower-semicontinuous tracial weights determines a separable nuclear C∗-algebra after tensoring with the Razak–Jacelon algebra and the compact operators

quote_B.text: answering Robert's trace-cone classification question positively

notes: Classification theorem (invariant determines the algebra up to isomorphism); could be coded M1 as a bare implication or M5 since the converse is trivial. Robert's question also appears as STW Problem LXVIII (survey repeat → P2 per tie-break 8). Lean comparator TraceIdealTransportSupport only formalizes supporting ideal/trace-weight lemmas (ideal lattice transport under a cone isomorphism), not the classification.

claim_formal: ∀ infinite compact metrizable X ∀ minimal homeomorphism h of X: rc(C(X) ⋊_h ℤ) = ½ mdim(X,h) in [0,∞]

quote_A.text: Let h be a minimal homeomorphism of an infinite compact metrizable space X. Then rc(C(X)⋊_hZ)=\frac12 mdim(X,h) in [0,∞].

quote_B.text: We prove the integer-action case of the Phillips–Toms conjecture

notes: B ambiguous: the integer-action formulation is posed as its own problem (Elliott–Niu; STW Problem XXXVI) → O1, but Niu's broader formulation for free minimal amenable-group actions makes this a restricted case (O5). Prior upper bounds supply one inequality. Corollary: zero mdim ⇔ SBP ⇔ Z-stable ⇔ dim_nuc<∞ ⇔ dim_nuc ≤ 1 for these crossed products. Companion manuscript proves a complex-cobordism filtered-product/compression theorem used for the lower bound.

claim_formal: ∀ complex C*-algebra C: (∀ h ∈ C_+, h properly infinite) → C strongly purely infinite (indeed ∀ a,b ∈ C_+ ∀ c ∀ ε ∃ s,t: ‖s*as−a‖,‖t*bt−b‖,‖s*ct‖ < ε)

quote_A.text: We prove that every complex C∗-algebra in which each positive element is properly infinite is strongly purely infinite.

quote_B.text: This answers the ordinary-to-strong part of Kirchberg–Rørdam's comparison question.

notes: Kirchberg–Rørdam Question 9.5 (also STW Problem LXXII) asks whether weak, ordinary and strong pure infiniteness agree in general and for nuclear algebras; the family settles ordinary⇒strong in general and weak⇒ordinary for exact algebras, so the general weak⇒ordinary part remains open (O5 also defensible). Corollary: separable nuclear weakly purely infinite algebras absorb O_∞. Lean IndividualStrongInfiniteness matches the headline; ExactInfiniteness covers the exact case.

claim_formal: ∀ n ≥ 1 ∀ connected Hausdorff second-countable topological n-manifold M (no boundary) ∀ locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group G acting faithfully and jointly continuously on M: G is a Lie group

quote_A.text: A locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group acting faithfully and jointly continuously on a connected Hausdorff second-countable topological n-manifold without boundary is a Lie group.

quote_B.text: We prove the Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every finite dimension

notes: Core new theorem: p-adic exclusion (every action of ℤ_p on a connected n-manifold has nonzero kernel, an M4-type statement); the full group statement follows by the classical Montgomery–Zippin/Yamabe reduction (prior results). Corollary: Pardon's Conjecture 1.4 on almost periodic homeomorphisms. Conjecture is stated for manifolds without boundary (second-countable, Hausdorff), matching the headline; low dimensions (n ≤ 3) were known.

claim_formal: ∃ compact oriented smooth 4-manifold M, ∃ generically immersed discs f_1..f_k with embedded boundaries and framed algebraic dual spheres g_i (λ(f_i,g_j)=δ_ij, λ(g_i,g_j)=0, μ̃(g_i)=0) such that the boundary circles bound no pairwise disjoint locally flat embedded discs

quote_A.text: We construct a compact oriented smooth four-manifold containing finitely many disc maps with framed algebraic dual spheres whose boundary circles bound no disjoint locally flat discs.

quote_B.text: We disprove the four-dimensional disc embedding conjecture without a fundamental-group hypothesis

notes: Corollaries: F_2 (and any group containing it) is not good in the Freedman–Quinn sense, answering the long-open free-group goodness question negatively; unrestricted topological surgery and s-cobordism cannot both hold. Third manuscript: a finitely presented PD_4 group with finite K(G,1) not the fundamental group of any closed aspherical topological 4-manifold, answering Wall's realization question (Wall Problem G2 / Davis Q3.4 / Lück Conj. 7.29) negatively (also M3/O2).

claim_formal: ∀ nontrivial smooth knot K ⊂ S³ ∀ slopes r, s ∈ ℚ ∪ {∞}: S³_r(K) ≅⁺ S³_s(K) → r = s

quote_A.text: Distinct Dehn surgery slopes on a nontrivial smooth knot never give orientation-preservingly homeomorphic manifolds.

quote_B.text: We prove the purely cosmetic surgery conjecture for knots in the three-sphere.

notes: Matrix M4 (non-existence of purely cosmetic pairs) vs M1 (implication homeomorphic ⇒ equal slopes). Proof finishes the last case (genus-two knots, slopes ±2) left by Hanselman and Daemi–Lidman–Miller Eismeier; meridional slope via Gordon–Luecke. Also Kirby list Problem 1.81(A) (Bleiler), so P3 is defensible; coded P1 as a named conjecture.

claim_formal: ∃ coarse disjoint union X = ⊔ X_j of finite connected graphs of uniformly bounded degree (uniformly discrete, bounded geometry) ∃ α ∈ KX_1(X) of infinite order with μ_X^max(α) = 0 (so μ_X^max ⊗ ℚ is not injective)

quote_A.text: There exist finite connected graphs (X_j) with a common finite bound on vertex degree, a coarse disjoint union X, and an infinite-order class α∈KX_1(X) such that μ_X^max(α)=0.

quote_B.text: We disprove the coarse Novikov conjecture: ordinary coarse assembly need not be rationally injective for uniformly discrete spaces of bounded geometry.

notes: Headline (title/summary) is the maximal coarse assembly kernel; since the maximal index maps to the reduced index, it implies the companion's disproof of the rational coarse Novikov conjecture (reduced assembly), which is the named posed problem. Lean comparator CoarseAssembly formalizes the reduced-assembly counterexample (constructedCoarseAssembly α = 0), hence 'weaker' than the maximal headline.

claim_formal: ∀ n ≥ 0 ∃ prime p ∃ finite p-local spectrum X: BP_*X ≅ BP_*/(p, v_1, …, v_n) as BP_*BP-comodules (canonical coaction, generator in degree 0)

quote_A.text: For every integer n≥0, there exist a prime p and a finite p-local spectrum X such that BP_*X≅BP_*/(p,v_1,…,v_n)

quote_B.text: Thus the all-height Smith--Toda existence problem has a positive answer when the prime may depend on the height.

notes: B ambiguous: the Smith–Toda realization problem is usually posed per (n,p) and is false at some pairs (Nave); the family answers the 'some prime for each height' form (O1 for that form, or O5 viewed as a partial answer to the per-prime problem). Companion manuscript: explicit V(4) at p = 1009, where V(4) existence had been recorded as open at every prime (Culver–Zhang) — that is an M2 existence with specific_instance, settling that open question.

claim_formal: At p = 3, ∀ j ≥ 0: (b_j ∈ Ext^{2,4·3^{j+1}} survives nontrivially to E_∞ in the mod-3 Adams SS) ⇔ j ∈ {0,2,3}, and each surviving coset contains an element of order 3 (K = K_3 = {0,2,3}; stems 10, 106, 322)

quote_A.text: At the prime three, K=K_3={0,2,3}. ... The class b_1 and every b_j with j≥4 fail to survive.

quote_B.text: We solve the Kervaire invariant problem at the prime three for the standard Kervaire classes in the mod-three Adams spectral sequence.

notes: Complete determination of the surviving index set (M6; M9 also defensible as an exact determination). Prefix could be 'none' since p=3 and the family b_j are fixed named objects; coded ∀ over j. B: the odd-primary Kervaire problem is posed for all odd primes; if p=3 is regarded as one case of a general problem, tie-break 6 gives O5 with restricted_range; coded O1 because p ≥ 5 is classically settled (Ravenel) so p=3 is the posed open case — low confidence. Corollaries: H-space decompositions of ΩS^{2n+1}{3} and homotopy-associativity of Anick spaces exactly for n ∈ {3,27,81}.

claim_formal: ∀ finite group G ∀ prime p: O_p(G) = 1 → H̃_*(A_p(G); ℚ) ≠ 0 (hence A_p(G) is not contractible)

quote_A.text: For every finite group G and every prime p, if O_p(G)=1, then H̃_*(A_p(G);Q)≠0.

quote_B.text: We prove Quillen's conjecture for all finite groups and all primes.

notes: Proves the stronger rational-homology form of Quillen's 1978 conjecture. Relies on the Aschbacher–Smith / Piterman–Smith / Piterman reductions; the odd-prime rational form had been deduced by Díaz Ramos (2026), so the genuinely new part is p = 2 (remaining characteristic-two/unitary cases). Could be read M4 (non-contractibility) but the headline is the homology non-vanishing implication.

claim_formal: ∀ prime p ∀ n ≥ 1 ∀ open U ⊆ A_n^×: the U-invariant proper prime ideals of E_0 = W(F_{p^n})[[u_1..u_{n−1}]] are exactly 0, I_1, …, I_n; hence the thick tensor ideals of dualizable K(n)-local spectra are exactly the chain D_0 ⊋ D_1 ⊋ … ⊋ D_{n+1} = 0

quote_A.text: The proper prime ideals of E_0 stabilized by U are precisely 0, I_1,…,I_n.

quote_B.text: This proves Chai's invariant-ideal conjecture in the standard finite-residue-field formulation. It also proves the Hovey–Strickland conjecture

notes: Two named conjectures: Chai's invariant-ideal hope (main arithmetic step) and Hovey–Strickland (via the Barthel–Heard–Naumann implication, a prior result; Balmer spectrum is a chain of n+1 points). Both are classifications (M6) with prefix ∀ and outcome O1.

claim_formal: ∀ Grothendieck coherator C (Ara–Henry convention): the homotopy theory of weak C-∞-groupoids (canonical semi-model structure) is equivalent to the homotopy theory of spaces; key step: ∀ cellular C-∞-groupoid X ∀ n ∀ cell a: D_n → X, the elementary expansion X → X⁺ is a weak equivalence

quote_A.text: its weak globular infinity-groupoids recover the homotopy theory of spaces

quote_B.text: We prove the Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis for every Grothendieck coherator in the Ara–Henry convention ... We also resolve Henry's pushout conjecture

notes: Main stated theorem is Henry's pushout conjecture (elementary expansions are weak equivalences, M1, P1/O1); the homotopy hypothesis follows via Henry's prior reduction to the semi-model structure. Lean comparator GrothendieckElementaryExpansion formalizes the pushout/elementary-expansion statement, an intermediate result relative to the homotopy-hypothesis headline. 'Ara–Henry convention' is the standard Maltsiniotis-style formulation, so O1 rather than O5.

claim_formal: ∀ prime p ∀ n ≥ 1 ∀ t ∈ ℤ: π_t L_{K(n)} S is a finitely generated ℤ_p-module (equivalently for L_{K(n)}F, F finite p-local)

quote_A.text: For every prime p, every integer n≥1, and every integer t, the Z_p-module π_t L_{K(n)}S_p^∧ is finitely generated.

quote_B.text: This answers the degreewise finiteness question of Hovey and Hovey–Strickland.

notes: Hovey / Hovey–Strickland question (no predicted answer stated in the input; could be read as a conjecture → P1).

claim_formal: ∀ prime p ∀ finite p-group G ∀ H ≤ G ∀ n ≥ 0: r_n(G,H) = ℓ(G,H) (optimal chromatic fixed-point loss equals the shortest cyclic subnormal chain length; sharp, witnessed by finite G-spectra)

quote_A.text: For every prime p, finite p-group G, subgroup H≤G, and integer n≥0, r_n(G,H)=ℓ(G,H).

quote_B.text: The equality holds at every prime and every nonnegative height, resolving positively the equality proposed by Kuhn and Lloyd.

notes: Upper bound r_n ≤ ℓ is the known cyclic chromatic Smith theorem; the new content is the matching lower bound (sharpness), so M9 (sharp value with attainment). Kuhn–Lloyd 'proposed equality' treated as a conjecture (P1); P2 possible if read as an open question.

claim_formal: ∀ finite connected aspherical integral Poincaré complex Q of formal dimension 4 (any orientation character): b_p^{(2)}(Q̃) = 0 for all p ≠ 2 (in particular for every closed connected aspherical topological 4-manifold)

quote_A.text: Let Q be a finite connected aspherical integral Poincaré complex of formal dimension four, with arbitrary orientation character. Then b_p^{(2)}(Q̃)=0 (p≥0, p≠2).

quote_B.text: We prove the four-dimensional Singer conjecture

notes: Singer conjecture is posed in every dimension; settling dimension 4 → O5 with restricted_range per tie-break 6 (O1 if the dimension-four case is taken as its own posed problem). Strengthened to Poincaré complexes (Lück's formulation). Corollaries: χ(M) ≥ 0, χ(M) ≥ |σ(M)|, Betti-number growth along towers.
